Name: Jan Hus
Summary: Bohemian priest and preacher at Bethlehem Chapel in Prague who criticised indulgences, clerical corruption and abuses of church power; he was burned at the stake at the Council of Constance in 1415 despite a safe-conduct.
Contribution: His preaching and writing, influenced by Wycliffe, fuelled the Bohemian reform, promoted Czech preaching and Scripture, and gave rise to the Hussite movement that outlived him by centuries.
Testimony: He refused to recant beliefs he held to be scriptural and went to the stake trusting in Christ, becoming a martyr of conscience for his followers.
